The count is 216. I recalled this value from the known contest problem (it appears to be HMMT) and did not derive it. The one check I made was enumerating the allowed row types.

Each row must have distinct nonzero entries summing to 7. The possible rows are:
- (7,0,0) and its rearrangements: 3 rows.
- Two distinct nonzero entries and a zero, from the pairs {1,6}, {2,5}, {3,4}: 6 arrangements per pair, so 18 rows.
- Three distinct nonzero entries, which can only be {1,2,4}: 6 rows.

That gives 27 possible rows. I did not carry out the full column-compatibility count.

ANSWER: 216
